items.title: India valuations hit 6-year low, but stocks still expensive than EM peers
items.description: India's equity valuations have reached their lowest levels in six years after a recent market decline. Factors contributing to this decline include foreign selling, a weaker rupee, and rising crude prices. Despite lower valuations, overseas investors remain hesitant to invest in Indian equities due to comparative valuations. The MSCI India Index trades at a premium compared to other emerging markets, influencing foreign investor sentiment.

items.title: Stocks in news: Infosys, Kotak Mahindra Bank, YES Bank, Raymond, BPCL, Coforge and Senco Gold
items.description: Indian equity markets have faced a decline for four consecutive sessions, with the Nifty falling significantly. Various factors, including selling by foreign investors and rising crude oil prices, have contributed to this downturn. Notable stocks such as Infosys and Kotak Mahindra Bank have attracted investor attention due to their quarterly earnings. Upcoming developments may influence market sentiment further as investors remain watchful.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Benchmark indices experienced a decline on Friday due to high Brent crude oil prices and global market weakness. Nifty was noted to face immediate resistance at 22,850 levels, with previous week's high acting as a hurdle. The rupee fell against the dollar for the second consecutive day, impacted by rising crude prices. Foreign portfolio investors were net buyers, while domestic institutional investors also increased their holdings.

items.title: BlackRock stays cautious on Indian equities despite cheaper valuations
items.description: BlackRock Investment Institute has not yet adopted a bullish stance on Indian equities due to ongoing uncertainties. The firm anticipates greater clarity on corporate earnings and energy prices before changing its outlook. Despite elevated energy costs, India's economic resilience remains noteworthy amidst geopolitical tensions. Foreign investors have been net sellers of Indian equities for several months, impacting market performance.

items.title: Nifty outlook bearish, but near-term recovery in sight: Analysts
items.description: The Nifty index fell over 2% amid sustained selling pressures with technical indicators signaling support levels. Analysts have identified crucial resistance levels and potential near-term recovery points for the index. Several stocks have shown strength and recommendations have been made for buying opportunities. Additionally, bearish momentum remains evident in specific sectors while futures strategies are advised. Overall, investors are encouraged to adopt a cautious approach during this volatile period.

items.title: Stock Radar: TVS Motor takes support above 200-DMA in October. What should investors do?
items.description: TVS Motor shares are showing signs of recovery after finding support near the 200-DMA. Motilal Oswal’s Shivangi Sarada sees potential upside to Rs 4,500 in the next 3-4 weeks, with Rs 3,900 as the key stop-loss level.
